_comment: What was done about each finding of the baseline scan. Keyed the same way the comparison keys them: package plus CVE list when there is one, otherwise category plus title. Written by hand after the fix, because only a person can say what was actually done. The first words decide the status shown in the report: "Fixed", "False positive", "No defect", or anything else for open.
dependency:@faker-js/faker: Fixed. The development dependency @faker-js/faker was upgraded from 9.9.0 to 10.6.0, the first release that closes the arbitrary code execution in helpers.fake. It is a major upgrade: the five APIs the project uses (internet.email, internet.password, person.fullName, seed, string.uuid) were checked and all three suites passed with no code change.
dependency:qs: Fixed. qs 6.15.3 arrived transitively through express 5.2.1 and through supertest. Neither had published a release carrying the fix, so 6.16.0 was forced across the whole tree with an override in package.json. npm audit went to zero vulnerabilities.
validator:CVE-2025-15104: False positive, reviewed and suppressed with a justification. CVE-2025-15104 describes an SSRF in Nu Html Checker (validator.nu), a Java service that fetches URLs on behalf of its callers. The npm package validator is a string validation library that makes no network access at all. Dependency-Check reached the finding by matching the package name against cpe:2.3:a:validator:validator, which is the CPE of the Java product. The suppression is in security/config/dependency-check-suppressions.xml with that analysis recorded.
dast:A Server Error response code was re: Fixed. There were five occurrences of HTTP 500, with two distinct causes. Four came from a NUL byte in a list filter (?name=%00, ?kind=%00, ?role=%00): PostgreSQL cannot store or compare \0 inside a text value and answers with an error, which surfaced as a 500. RejectNullBytesPipe was added, registered as a global APP_PIPE, refusing the input with a 400 before any query (src/shared/presentation/pipes/reject-null-bytes.pipe.ts). The fifth came from GET /vehicles?customerId=..., which took the raw string into a uuid column; the parameter now uses ParseUUIDPipe, as every other route in the project already did. Verified after the fix: both requests now answer 400.
dast:Application Error Disclosure: Fixed by the same change. The alert was a consequence of the 500 on GET /vehicles?customerId=customerId, not a separate defect: with no 500 there is no error response to disclose. The route now validates the identifier and answers 400.
dast:Information Disclosure - Debug Erro: Fixed by the same change. The "Internal server error" body ZAP captured came from the same 500 on GET /vehicles?customerId=customerId. With the parameter validated, the response became a 400 that names the invalid field, without revealing that something broke underneath.
dast:Non-Storable Content: Fixed at the point that mattered, though the alert remains by construction. The API answered with no cache directive at all, and its responses carry personal data: documents, addresses, phone numbers, user roles. With no directive, each intermediate cache decides for itself whether to store them, which is the weakness in CWE-524. A middleware was added that sets Cache-Control: no-store and Pragma: no-cache on every response (src/shared/presentation/no-store.middleware.ts). ZAP raises this alert precisely when content is not storable, so it keeps appearing: now describing the intended behaviour rather than an accident.
dast:A Client Error response code was re: Analysed. The occurrences were broken down by status code: most were 401 and 429 caused by the scan itself, not by the application. The 401s came from ZAP calling routes that revoke the user's session (DELETE /auth/sessions and POST /users/me/password), destroying the token it was authenticated with; those routes are now removed from the definition that drives the scan. The 429s were the rate limiter working: it answered 72% of the scan traffic, and the limit was raised in the scan environment to obtain real coverage. The remaining 400s and 404s are correct answers from the API to an invalid payload and to a non-existent identifier.
dast:Private IP Disclosure: No defect. GET /auth/sessions returns the user their own list of active sessions, with the source address of each one. That is what lets someone recognise a session they did not open, and it is the pattern any service offering session management adopts. The address ZAP flagged (172.19.0.1) is the gateway of the local Docker network, an artefact of the test environment. This finding only appeared once the scan started authenticating, because the route is protected.
dast:Authentication Request Identified: No defect. This is ZAP identifying POST /auth/sessions and POST /users as authentication routes, to steer its own rules. Informational by construction.
dast:Session Management Response Identif: No defect. This is ZAP recognising the API's session format from the OpenAPI specification. Informational by construction.
